Targ. Y. Deut. V, 5 למִתְנְיָא (ed. Vien. למִתַּנְיָא Ithpe.); a. fr.—Esp. (denom. of מתניתא) to teach or study Mishnah or Boraitha; in gen. to report a tradition, teach, study.
<cite ref="Eruvin 36b:9">Erub. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>ליתא למתניתן מדתָנֵי איו דת׳ איו וכ׳</he> our Mishnah is no authority, as it is contradicted by what Ayo teaches, for Ayo taught &c.

<cite ref="Yoma 27b:9">Yoma 27ᵇ</cite> <he>והא אנן לא תְּנָן הכי</he> but we have not so learned in the Mishnah! <cite ref="Yoma 27b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>הך … קתני הך … לא קתני</he> the Mishnah speaks of that which, if neglected, can be remedied; that which cannot be remedied it does not mention.

<cite ref="Shabbat 2a:7">Sabb. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>תנן התם וכ׳</he> there (in the Mishnah, <cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 1:1">Shebu. I, 1</cite>) we read &c. Ib.ᵇ <he>מאי שנא הכא דת׳ … ומ״ש התם דת׳ וכ׳</he> why does the Mishnah here read …, and there &c.? <cite ref="Berakhot 8b:23">Ber. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>תְּנִינָא וכ׳</he> we are taught in the Mishnah &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 2a:6">Ib. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>דקת׳ מאימתי</he>, v. <cite ref="S00007"><he>קָאֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 2a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>כדתַנְיָא</he> as it is stated (in the Boraitha).
Yoma 26ᵃ לכדתניא (the word peder is needed) to intimate the law taught in the Boraitha.
<cite ref="Yoma 26a:8">Ib.</cite> <he>והתניא וכ׳</he> but has it not been taught &c.?; <cite ref="Yoma 28a:7">ib. 28ᵃ</cite>, a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 28a:17">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>והתניא</he> and so it has been taught.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Challah 2:1:12">Y. Ḥall. II, 58ᶜ</cite> <he>ר׳ יונה ת׳ דר״ש וכ׳</he> R. Jonah taught (and adopted) the opinion of R. S. b. J.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:1:19">Y. Kidd. I, 58ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>תמן תנינן</he> there (in a Mishnah) we read &c.

<cite ref="Megillah 24b:18">Meg. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>לימא תנינן להא דתָנוּ רבנן וכ׳</he> shall we say that we are here taught that which the Rabbis have taught &c. (i.e. is this a confirmation of what &c.)?—

<cite ref="Berakhot 13a:2">Ber. 13ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>תָּנוּ רבנן</he> (abbrev. <he>ת״ר</he>) the Rabbis have taught (introducing a discussion); a. v. fr.—[In Talm. Babli <he>תנן</he> refers to Mishnah, <he>תניא</he> to Boraitha.]

Ber. 49ᵃ ברכת … וחַנּוּיֵי קא מְתַנִּינָא Ms. M. (or מַתְנִינָא Af.; ed. מְתַנִּינָן or מַתְנִינָן) I have not learned the benediction over food, and shall I teach (Mishnah)?
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 4:24">Targ. Y. Ex. IV, 24</cite>.—

<cite ref="Ketubot 3a:11">Keth. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון דאיבעי ליה לאַתְנוּיֵי ולא א׳ וכ׳</he> because he ought to have made it a condition (not to count so common an obstacle as the absence of a ferry), and he did not make it, he has to take the consequences.

<cite ref="Shevuot 11b:9">Shebu. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>וכי קיימי ב״ד ומַתְנוּ משום עורה</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>וקיימי ב״ד ומתנו אדעתא דעורה</he>) did the court establish a general law (that dead sacrificial animals need not be redeemed,) and stipulate that it must be redeemed for the value of its skin?; a. e.

<cite ref="Berakhot 8b:23">Ber. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>איכא דמַתְנֵי להא וכ׳</he> some one quoted that opinion of R. A. bar Ḥ. with reference to what has been taught, ‘R. S. b. Y. says &c.’ <cite ref="Ketubot 17a">Keth. 17ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>וה״מ למאן דקרי ותני אבל למאן דמתני וכ׳</he> this has been said concerning the funeral only of one who was versed in Bible and a student of Mishnah, but as regards one who was a teacher of Mishnah, there is no limit (of attendance at his funeral).

<cite ref="Chullin 48a:4">Ḥull. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>הא … אתון אהא מַתְנִיתוּן לה אנן אדרבא מַתְנִינָן לה</he> you report that action of R. N. … in connection with this, we report it in connection with what Raba said &c.; a. fr.
